audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects states it outright: the chart gives Irelia 4 of 7 stages and Zaahen 0, while Irelia wins only 45.55% of 1405 games. Every prose why says Irelia owns first item and 2+ items too.
audit.why: Zaahen's kit is what a losing late game looks like for Irelia: Aureate Rush (E) deals percent-health so her armour builds do not answer it, The Darkin Glaive (Q) heals on a 6s max-rank cooldown, Grim Deliverance (R) heals for a portion of the damage it deals, and Determination gives him bonus AD and a revive at full stacks. Her real edge is the level 2-3 stun-and-reset window before any of that exists.
audit.corrected: Skill, Irelia, Irelia, Zaahen, Zaahen, Skill, Zaahen — Irelia 2, Zaahen 3, Skill 2, consistent with a sub-50% win rate. Proposed as matched full/content pairs with ratings and the whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[] has 3 entries where 4 are expected — the late-game spike is simply absent, and it is the one that matters most here.
audit.why: Determination is the scaling mechanic: 'When filled with Determination, Zaahen gains increased Attack Damage and can revive.' A player who does not know he revives will lose a fight he already won.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] created with before:null — the Determination revive and bonus AD at 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one of Zaahen's abilities is named anywhere on the page — every reference is 'Ultimate', 'his key spell', 'his combo'. Three concrete interactions were missing entirely: the Q auto-reset and its knock-up recast, the percent-health E, and the double heal on Q and R.
audit.why: Riot text — Q: 'slashes twice on his next attack, dealing bonus damage and healing himself. Zaahen can recast this ability to have his next attack deal bonus damage and knock up his target' (10/9/8/7/6s, auto reset). W: 'stabs in a direction, damaging enemies hit, then pulls them toward him' (14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, 850 range). E Aureate Rush: dash and slice, flagged percentHealth (10/9.5/9/8.5/8s). R Grim Deliverance: 'damaging enemies and healing for a portion of the damage dealt' (110/95/80s).
audit.corrected: Do's and Don'ts now name Grim Deliverance's 110s rank-1 cooldown and its heal, the Q auto-reset with its knock-up recast, and Aureate Rush's percent-health damage as the reason armour is the wrong buy.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, sequencingCues 0.
audit.why: Every trade decision here keys off whether Grim Deliverance (110/95/80s) and the W pull (12-14s) are available.
audit.corrected: Do's now reads as an explicit wait-for-X-before-Y line with the real number.

audit.whatIsWrong: The item line has no anti-heal at all, and leans on Plated Steelcaps against a champion whose E is percent-health.
audit.why: Two of his four abilities heal him; Aureate Rush ignores the value of stacked armour.
audit.corrected: Recorded here rather than edited — the item string is shared boilerplate and an anti-heal insertion belongs with the owner's item pass.

notes: This matchup carried four packet defects and all four are addressed. The chart rewrite is the one judgement call: the packet's own chart is flagged as contradicting the data (Irelia 4/7 at a 45.55% win rate), so I could not simply copy it — the new chart is derived from Zaahen's kit (percent-health E, two heals, Determination revive) and keeps Irelia's genuine 2-3 window. Confidence Medium on the exact row placement for 4-5 versus 6; the direction is not in doubt. Zaahen's W has no name in either the kit file or the missing-interactions file, so it is referred to as 'the W pull' rather than guessed. packet.defects' suspect name "Flawless Duet's" is a FALSE POSITIVE — correct name with a possessive.
